text:
Nora Patel: FYI OrionHealth submitted a formal SLA credit request for March sustained latency on dedicated tier (INV-2026-03-99 attached). They say latency > 250ms for 4h on Mar 19 and want the SLA credit + burst charge reconciliation.
Evan Reed: saw their ticket (SUP-6344). Eng-SRE alerted on Mar19 at 02:10 UTC about degraded p99. quick check shows autoscaler struggled during an OS roll patch.
Sophie Tran: can we get the invoice lines? need to separate reserved commit charges vs burst.
Nora Patel: pulled PDF -> relevant bits:
```
Line 10: Reserved - OrionHealth - 1.0 GPU-month - Mar1-31 = $12,000
Line 55: Burst overage - GPU hours (Mar19 00:00-06:00) = 24.0 hrs = $2,880
Line 98: SLA credit applied? 0.0 (customer dispute requests retrocredit)
Invoice total: $14,880
```
Jules Kramer: eng-sre timeline: 2026-03-19T01:58Z kernel patch started on node pool-east-7; 02:10Z high p99 observed; 02:45Z rollback started; 03:30Z remediation complete. Impact window ~72 minutes p99 > 250ms.
Evan Reed: vendor note - we had 2 borrowed GPUs for burst from partner cluster during that window; partner reported higher queueing delays because their provisioning API throttled. That likely amplified the latency.
Sophie Tran: SLA policy: for Dedicated, credit = proportion of time SLA missed * monthly reserved fee for that model. For p99 target 200ms missed for ~1.2h => credit = (1.2h / (24*31h)) * reserved_month_fee? need exact formula.
Nora Patel: I pulled policy doc: monthly credit = (minutes_of_violation / total_minutes_in_month) * reserved_commit_month_fee. Total minutes in March = 44640. Violation = 72 minutes. So credit = 72/44640 * $12,000 = $19.38 -> seems tiny. But customer argues the burst charges during the incident should be waived since they resulted from failover behavior.
Jules Kramer: tech POV: some requests were rerouted to burst pool causing extra GPU hours (approx 10 GPU-hours) while primary nodes under backlog. That produced the $2,880 line for other bursts too.
Evan Reed: recommendation: apply SLA credit per policy (small $19.38) but also consider a discretionary goodwill refund for the burst overage portion that was outside customer's control. propose waiving 8 of 10 GPU-hours (~$960). Total proposed credit ~$980.
Sophie Tran: need finance approval for discretionary credit > $500. Prepare package with logs, incident timeline, and partner API throttling note.
Nora Patel: @billing-bot create request ADJ-2026-4510 with artifacts: SUP-6344, incident-log-03-19.json, partner-throttle-report.pdf, invoice-copy. Flag discretionary amount $960.
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4510 created. Artifacts attached. Status: pending-discretionary-approval.
Sophie Tran: Evan, can you produce simple calc lines for the approval doc? itemize: SLA credit $19.38, burst waiver $960, net credit $979.38. Also include cost impact to us (partner pass-through and internal cost).
Evan Reed: calc attached in ADJ-2026-4510: SLA credit 72/44640*$12,000 = $19.38; burst waiver 8 GPU-hrs * $120/hr = $960; total customer credit $979.38. Our cost: partner billed 10 GPU-hrs at $70/hr -> $700; we'll absorb $560 of that if we waive 8 hours (we can recoup 2 hrs).
Jules Kramer: recommend we absorb the goodwill as customer is enterprise with renewed commit next quarter. Also note we should open partner dispute for throttling penalty.
Sophie Tran: approving up to $1,000 discretionary credit here. Finance lead signoff required for > $1,000. This is below that. I'll mark as approved.
Nora Patel: thanks. @billing-bot please update ADJ-2026-4510 status to approved_by_finance_ops and schedule for Apr billing cycle. Add customer note: "SLA credit applied per policy; one-time goodwill waiver applied to burst overage."
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4510 status updated: approved_by_finance_ops. Scheduled for billing run 2026-04-03. Journal entry JE-2026-7821 created. Customer notification drafted.
Evan Reed: filing follow-up action: open partner dispute ticket PD-212 for throttling; product to add alert when partner API throttles during critical windows.
Sophie Tran: internal note: this is a datapoint for our SLA language - the math shows tiny credits for short p99 blips. will propose adding a minimum credit floor for >30min incidents to be more meaningful.
Nora Patel: noted. I'll coordinate customer comms with Jules. Closing loop here unless anyone objects.
Jules Kramer: no objections. Customer comms ready.
billing-bot: Customer email sent to OrionHealth: credit $979.38 applied to next invoice; incident summary attached.
Nora Patel: thread closed. :white_check_mark:
